questions.question: Karim finds that 30% of patients don't show up. Leila advises him:
options: Confirm by SMS the day before
questions.explanation: Dr. Leila: 'Karim, SMS reminders the day before reduce missed appointments by 50%. It's simple, fast, and effective. Install software that sends automatic reminders.'

questions.question: Patients are not loyal after the first visit. The cause is:
questions.explanation: Dr. Leila: 'Karim, loyalty is based on the relationship. A patient who feels heard and understood will return. Take the time to talk to them, to answer their questions.'

questions.question: To re-engage lost patients, Karim should:
questions.explanation: Dr. Leila: 'Karim, a simple call to check on a patient can be enough to bring them back. It's a professional and human gesture that patients appreciate.'

questions.question: A patient who doesn't show up costs Karim:
questions.explanation: Dr. Leila: 'Karim, a missed appointment represents a loss of time and money. The time you would have spent on another patient. That's why reminders are essential.'

questions.question: To reduce missed appointments, you should:
questions.explanation: Dr. Leila: 'Karim, systematic reminder the day before is the most effective method. Some practices also request a deposit for heavy procedures to reduce cancellations.'

questions.question: Karim has a loan of 800,000 DH. His average monthly payment is:
questions.explanation: Dr. Leila: 'Karim, for a loan of 800,000 DH over 7 years, monthly payments are about 10,000 to 15,000 DH depending on the interest rate. You need to factor this cost into your budget forecast.'

questions.question: Karim's fixed expenses mainly include:
questions.explanation: Dr. Leila: 'Karim, rent and insurance are fixed expenses. They are paid every month, even if you have no patients. You need to anticipate them.'

questions.question: The break-even point is reached when:
questions.explanation: Dr. Leila: 'Karim, the break-even point is reached when your revenue covers your fixed and variable expenses. It's the goal to achieve in the first months.'

questions.question: To reduce his expenses, Karim can:
questions.explanation: Dr. Leila: 'Karim, negotiating with suppliers is a good practice. Ask for discounts, compare prices, and group your purchases. Every dirham saved is important.'

questions.question: Monthly cash flow monitoring allows you to:
questions.explanation: Dr. Leila: 'Karim, rigorous cash flow monitoring allows you to anticipate overdrafts and manage your expenses. Use a spreadsheet or accounting software.'

questions.question: Karim must declare his activity to the ONMD within:
questions.explanation: Dr. Leila: 'Karim, you must declare your activity to the ONMD within 15 days of opening. It's a legal obligation that can lead to sanctions in case of delay.'

questions.question: The commercial lease must be registered with the:
questions.explanation: Dr. Leila: 'Karim, the commercial lease must be registered with the tax office within 30 days of signing. This makes it enforceable against third parties.'

questions.question: Fees must be displayed:
questions.explanation: Dr. Leila: 'Karim, displaying fees is mandatory and must be visible in the waiting room. It's an ethical and legal obligation that avoids misunderstandings.'

questions.question: In case of a dispute with a patient, Karim should:
options: Refer the matter to the Order's council
questions.explanation: Dr. Leila: 'Karim, in case of a dispute, you should first try to resolve it amicably. If that's not possible, the Order's council can be contacted for mediation.'

questions.question: The best way to attract patients is:
questions.explanation: Dr. Leila: 'Karim, word of mouth is your best asset. Ask your first patients to talk about you. Offer a small commercial gesture to those who bring you a new patient.'

questions.question: To retain a patient, you mainly need:
questions.explanation: Dr. Leila: 'Karim, loyalty is built on a trusting relationship. Listening, empathy, and quality of care are the pillars of loyalty.'

questions.question: Patients come back when they feel:
questions.explanation: Dr. Leila: 'Karim, a patient who feels heard and respected will return. Take the time to understand their needs and answer their questions.'

questions.question: A satisfied patient can bring:
questions.explanation: Dr. Leila: 'Karim, a satisfied patient will bring up to 5 new patients on average. It's the best marketing investment you can make.'

questions.question: To stand out, Karim should offer:
questions.explanation: Dr. Leila: 'Karim, quality of care is what will make the difference. Patients are looking for a competent and humane dentist, not the cheapest one.'

questions.question: Karim is stressed by the first months. Leila advises him:
options: Take a step back and breathe
questions.explanation: Dr. Leila: 'Karim, taking a step back is essential in times of stress. Take 5 minutes to breathe, reassess the situation, and act serenely.'

questions.question: Work-life balance mainly allows:
questions.explanation: Dr. Leila: 'Karim, work-life balance is the key to avoiding burnout and maintaining a sustainable professional activity in the long term.'

questions.question: To stay motivated, Karim should:
questions.explanation: Dr. Leila: 'Karim, each loyal patient, each month with a positive balance, is a victory. Celebrate them to stay motivated.'

questions.question: Resilience is the ability to:
questions.explanation: Dr. Leila: 'Karim, resilience is a key skill for a young doctor. It's your ability to bounce back after difficulties and come out stronger.'

questions.question: To overcome this period, Karim should:
questions.explanation: Dr. Leila: 'Karim, you are not alone. Surround yourself with colleagues, family, and mentors. Support is essential to overcome crises.'

questions.question: After 6 months, Karim realizes that:
questions.explanation: Dr. Leila: 'Karim, beginnings are always difficult. But each passing month is a learning experience. Soon, you will have a loyal patient base and you will be able to breathe.'
